product.name: Zyra
product.headline: Every session covered.
product.description: Builds the roster around who is actually free, swaps sessions in two taps and reminds everyone before they're on. Free for small teams; works in any phone browser.

guides.title: Getting started: your first space in ten minutes
guides.standfirst: Create a space for your team, add a group for each roster, invite people with a code, and put the first sessions on the calendar.
guides.meta_title: Getting started with Zyra: your first roster | Zyra
guides.meta_description: Create a space, add groups, invite your team with a join code and add your first sessions — a ten-minute set-up for any volunteer or shift team.

blocks.title: The short version
blocks.text: Sign up, tap **New space**, invite people from the **People** tab, then add sessions on the **Roster** tab. Everyone sees their sessions as soon as you add them — there's no separate publish step.
The words Zyra uses

blocks.caption: A quick map before you start.
rows: Your organisation — a church, café, club or crew
A team inside the space, with its own roster, chat, notices and people
One rostered slot on the calendar
A role on a session, like Sound, Ushers or Barista

blocks.text: 1. Create your account

Open Zyra in any phone or computer browser and choose **Create your account**. You'll need a password of at least 12 characters, and you'll confirm your email with a link — open it on the same device.
2. Create a space

items: Go to **Spaces**, open the **+** menu and choose **New space**.
Give it a name, a short description and your time zone.
Name the first group (it starts as “Main group”) and pick a calendar type: **Roster** for many people at once, or **Exclusive** for one booking at a time, like a room or a van.
Leave **Leads approve swaps** on if you'd like a lead to check every swap.
Tap **Create space**.

blocks.text: 3. Invite your team

On the **People** tab, tap **Invite** and choose how many people the invite is for. Zyra gives you a six-character join code and a link to send however you like. See [Inviting people and choosing roles](/guides/zyra/inviting-people-and-roles) for the details.
4. Add the first sessions

On the **Roster** tab, tap **Add sessions**, pick the people, the position and the dates, and set it to repeat if it happens every week. [Building a fair roster](/guides/zyra/building-a-fair-roster) walks through it.

items.q: Is it free?
items.a: Yes for small teams. Each space is free up to a set number of people; larger spaces add seats. See [Plans, seats and Unlimited](/guides/zyra/plans-seats-and-unlimited).

items.q: Do people need to install an app?
items.a: No. Zyra works in any phone browser. Adding it to the home screen makes it feel like an app and lets it send notifications.

guides.title: Inviting people and choosing roles
guides.standfirst: Join codes, invite links, and what Members, Leads and Owners can each do — so the right people can change the roster and everyone else can simply turn up.
guides.meta_title: Invite your team and set roles in Zyra | Zyra
guides.meta_description: Create a join code or invite link, decide how many people it's for, and give each person the Member, Lead or Owner role.

blocks.title: The short version
blocks.text: **People** › **Invite** makes a join code and a link that last 7 days. Everyone joins as a Member; promote the people who run the roster to Lead.
Making an invite

items: Open your space and go to the **People** tab.
Tap **Invite** and choose how many people can use it: one person, up to 10, 50 or 200.
Tap **Create invite link**, then **Copy code**, **Copy link**, **Email invite** or **Share**.

blocks.text: The code and link are shown only once, so send them straight away. Links expire after 7 days. Codes are six characters and never use 0, O, 1 or I, so they're easy to read aloud at a meeting.
Joining
With a link, people tap it and choose **Join space**. With a code, they go to **Spaces**, open **+**, choose **Join with a code** and type it in.
Roles

blocks.caption: Change a role from **People** › the person › Role.
rows: See the roster, book themselves and swap sessions
Everything a Member can, plus manage the roster, approve swaps and post notices
Everything, including roles for everyone. One owner per space; hand it over when you step back

blocks.text: Owners and leads are in every group. To choose who else is in a group, open the group's people list and use **Add from the space** or **Take out** — taking someone out releases their upcoming sessions in that group.
When someone moves on

**Remove from space** on their profile cancels their upcoming sessions, so check the roster afterwards. If you're the owner and stepping back yourself, make someone else owner first — you become a lead.

items.q: Can members invite people too?
items.a: Yes, any active member can create an invite. Leads decide who gets which role.

items.q: What does “This space is full” mean?
items.a: The space has used all its seats. The person can tap **Let them know I'm waiting**, and the owner can add seats in Settings. People on Unlimited can always join.

guides.title: Asking for availability without the spreadsheet
guides.standfirst: Let people mark holidays and unavailable days themselves, so you see clashes while you roster instead of after.
guides.meta_title: Collect team availability for your roster | Zyra
guides.meta_description: How your team adds holidays and unavailable days in Zyra, how to import them from a file, and how leads see clashes while rostering.

blocks.title: The short version
blocks.text: Ask everyone to add their time off under **Availability and holidays**. When you roster someone who's away, Zyra warns you straight away.
For everyone on the team

items: Open **Availability and holidays**.
Tap **+** and choose **Add time off**.
Pick **Holiday** or **Unavailable**, whole days or a time range, and add a note if it helps.
Save. Only you and your leads can see it.

blocks.text: Already keep your holidays in a calendar? Use **Import from a file** with an .ics file, or **Download template** to fill in a spreadsheet and import it as .csv.
Space-wide holidays
Leads can add dates the whole space is closed on the **Holidays** tab — including public holidays — so nobody gets rostered on them by accident.
What leads see

When you add a session for someone who's away, Zyra warns you — for example “on holiday then” or “marked themselves unavailable”. It's a warning, not a block: sometimes a person is happy to come in anyway, and you stay in charge.
Getting people to actually fill it in

items: Ask once, with a date: “Please add your holidays for next term by Sunday.”
Post it as a notice on the **Notices** tab so it sits at the top of the space.
Roster after the deadline, and tell people that's how it works — it quickly becomes a habit.

items.q: Can other members see my time off?
items.a: No. Only you and your space's leads see it.

items.q: Does Zyra build the roster from availability automatically?
items.a: Not yet — automatic drafting is on the way. Today you add sessions yourself, with availability warnings shown as you go.

guides.title: Building a fair roster
guides.standfirst: Spread the work evenly, respect people's limits, and keep the same few volunteers from carrying everything. Here is how to do it in Zyra.
guides.meta_title: How to build a fair volunteer or shift roster | Zyra
guides.meta_description: Add sessions, set positions and rostering limits, and spot overloaded people early so the same few volunteers don't carry the whole roster.

blocks.title: The short version
blocks.text: Set your positions and rostering limits once in **Settings**, collect availability, then add sessions from the **Roster** tab. Zyra warns you when someone is away, over their limit or rostered on consecutive days, and blocks double bookings outright.
Set up once

items: **Positions** — the roles on a session (Sound, Welcome, Kids, Barista…). Members tick the ones they can do under “Your positions”.
**Rostering limits** — the most sessions per person per day or week, and whether to avoid consecutive days or consecutive weeks.
**Availability** — ask everyone to add their time off first. See [Asking for availability](/guides/zyra/asking-for-availability).

blocks.text: Adding sessions

items: On **Roster**, tap **Add sessions**.
Choose the group, then one or more people and the position.
Pick the dates: **One day**, **Date range** or **Pick days**, and a repeat if it's weekly.
Tap **Add session** (or **Add N sessions**). People see them immediately.

blocks.text: What makes a roster feel fair

Fair doesn't mean identical — it means nobody quietly does far more than everyone else, and people get a say in when. Rotate the less popular slots, pair new people with experienced ones, and keep an eye on who has said yes most often. The **Dashboard** tab gives owners and leads an overview of the space.
Warnings and blocks

blocks.caption: Zyra tells you, but leaves most decisions with you.
rows: Person is on holiday or unavailable
Over the most sessions per day or week
Warning, if you turned that limit on
Person not set up for the position
Same person already booked at that time

items.q: Can Zyra draft the roster for me?
items.a: Automatic drafting from everyone's availability is coming after launch. For now you place sessions, with Zyra's warnings guiding you.

items.q: Can I export the roster?
items.a: Owners and leads can export from the Dashboard as Excel or PDF.

guides.title: Weekly and recurring sessions
guides.standfirst: Sunday services, Saturday shifts, the first Monday of the month: set them up once and change one week without breaking the rest.
guides.meta_title: Set up weekly and recurring sessions | Zyra
guides.meta_description: Create repeating sessions in one go, pick specific days, and edit one session, this and following, or all upcoming without starting again.

blocks.title: The short version
blocks.text: In **Add sessions**, choose a repeat. Later, when you edit a session, choose whether the change applies to **This session**, **This and following** or **All upcoming**.
Creating a repeat

items: On **Roster**, tap **Add sessions** and fill in the group, people and position.
Set the first date, then open the repeat options — from “Don't repeat” through weekly patterns to **Custom…**.
Or use **Pick days** to tap the exact dates when there's no pattern.
Add them all at once. One batch can hold up to 62 sessions — plenty for a year of weekly sessions.

blocks.text: Changing one week

Tap the session, choose **Edit**, make the change, then pick **This session**. Only that date changes. Pick **This and following** when something changes for good from a date onward, like a new start time from next month.
Cancelling
**Cancel session** on a single date is for a one-off — a public holiday or a building closure. If the whole run is ending, edit with **All upcoming** instead.
Rotating people through a repeat

A rotation (different people each week) is easiest as several repeats: one per person or pair, each every second or fourth week. Zyra's double-booking check stops two repeats from landing the same person twice at the same time.

items.q: Do people get notified about every new session?
items.a: They see them on the roster straight away, and get reminders before each one — by default the day before.

items.q: Can I add one-off events too?
items.a: Yes — **Add event** puts something on the calendar that isn't a rostered session, like a team lunch.

blocks.title: Set it once. Change one week.
blocks.label: Open Zyra

guides.title: How Zyra prevents double bookings
guides.standfirst: Nobody can be in two places at once, and a room can't hold two bookings. Here is exactly what Zyra blocks, and what it only warns about.
guides.meta_title: How Zyra prevents double bookings | Zyra
guides.meta_description: What counts as a double booking in Zyra, how roster and exclusive calendars differ, and why swaps can't create clashes either.

blocks.title: The short version
blocks.text: Zyra refuses any session or swap that would put the same person in two overlapping sessions, and any overlapping booking on an **Exclusive** calendar. Everything else — holidays, limits, positions — is a warning you can choose to override.
Two kinds of calendar

blocks.caption: Chosen when you create a group.
rows: Teams where many people work at once
Different people can overlap; the same person can't
A room, a vehicle or a single slot
Only one booking at a time

blocks.text: What gets blocked

items: Adding a session that overlaps one the person already has on that calendar.
Accepting or approving a swap that would double-book someone — you'll see “That swap would double-book someone.”
A second booking at the same time on an Exclusive calendar.

blocks.text: The check runs in the database itself, not just on your screen, so two leads adding sessions at the same moment can't sneak a clash past it.
What only gets a warning
Holidays, “unavailable” days, rostering limits and positions produce warnings. They're real information, but there are good reasons to roster someone anyway, so the decision stays with the lead.

items.q: Can one person be in two different groups' sessions at the same time?
items.a: Each group has its own calendar, so check across groups yourself if people serve in more than one team.

items.q: Why can't a swap go through?
items.a: Most often because it would double-book the person taking it. Ask someone else, or adjust one of the sessions first.

guides.title: Swapping a session without the group chat
guides.standfirst: Can't make it? Offer your session to the whole space, ask one person directly, or trade with someone — and let Zyra keep the roster right.
guides.meta_title: Swap a shift or session without the group chat | Zyra
guides.meta_description: Offer a session to the space, ask a teammate to take it or trade sessions, how lead approval works, and when swap requests expire.

blocks.title: The short version
blocks.text: Tap your session, choose **Swap or hand over**, and either **Offer it to the space** (first to accept gets it) or pick a teammate. The roster updates by itself once it's accepted — and approved, if your space asks leads to approve swaps.
Giving away your session

items: Open the session on the **Roster** and tap **Swap or hand over**.
Choose **Offer it to the space**, or a teammate.
Add a note if it helps, then send it.
When someone accepts, the session moves to them.

blocks.text: Asking for someone else's session
Tap their session and choose **Ask to swap**. You can offer to **Take it over**, or offer one of your own sessions in return.
Answering and approving

Everything lives on the **Swaps** tab: **Needs your answer** (accept or decline), **Waiting for your approval** for leads, **Your requests** (withdraw any you no longer need) and **Recent**. If **Leads approve swaps** is on, a swap shows “Waiting for a lead” until a lead approves it.
When requests expire
A request lasts 48 hours, or until the session starts if that's sooner. Each session can only have one open request at a time, so offers never pile up.

items.q: Can a swap double-book someone?
items.a: No. Zyra checks before the swap goes through.

items.q: Can leads move people around directly?
items.a: Yes — leads have **Swap with…** on any session. Owners decide whether leads can also use it on their own sessions.

items.q: Will the lead know?
items.a: Leads can turn on **Tell me when swaps happen** in Settings.

guides.title: Covering sick leave at short notice
guides.standfirst: Someone wakes up unwell. Here is how they tell the team in a moment, how their sessions get offered for cover, and what everyone else sees.
guides.meta_title: Cover sick leave and absences quickly | Zyra
guides.meta_description: Report sick in Zyra, offer your sessions for cover automatically, and how leads mark someone absent and hand the session on.

blocks.title: The short version
blocks.text: On **Home**, tap **I'm sick**, choose how long, and tap **Tell my spaces**. Your sessions in that time are offered to others for cover. Tap **I'm back** when you're better.
If you're unwell

items: On **Home**, find “Feeling unwell?” and tap **I'm sick**.
Choose how long: today, or a few days (up to 14).
Add a note for your leads if you like.
Tap **Tell my spaces**.

blocks.text: Your sessions in that time are offered to the team — “On leave. Can you cover this shift?” — so you don't have to message anyone yourself.
Who sees what
Other members only see that you're on leave. Your leads see that it's sick leave, and your note. Health details stay between you and the people who run the roster.
For leads
If someone tells you directly, open their session and tap **Mark absent or sick**. Choose Absent or Sick leave, and optionally **Give this session to someone else** in the same step.
No-shows

If your space uses check-in, leads can be told when someone hasn't checked in 10 minutes after a session starts — early enough to find cover. See [QR or code check-in](/guides/zyra/qr-or-code-check-in).

items.q: What if nobody takes my session?
items.a: Your leads can see it's uncovered and reassign it.

items.q: Do I have to give a reason?
items.a: No. The note is optional, and only your leads see it.

guides.title: Reminders people actually read
guides.standfirst: Phone notifications, Telegram, and a personal nudge from a lead. Set them up once and people stop forgetting their sessions.
guides.meta_title: Session reminders people actually read | Zyra
guides.meta_description: Turn on phone notifications, connect Telegram, choose when reminders arrive, and send a teammate a gentle nudge before their session.

blocks.title: The short version
blocks.text: Add Zyra to your home screen, turn on **Send notifications here** under **Me**, and you'll get a reminder the day before each session. Prefer Telegram? Connect it in the same place.
1. Add Zyra to your home screen

blocks.caption: Notifications on iPhone need the home-screen icon (iOS 16.4 or later).
rows: In Safari, tap Share, then **Add to Home Screen**, then Add
Use the install icon in the address bar, or in Safari, File › Add to Dock

blocks.text: 2. Turn on notifications
Open Zyra from the home-screen icon, go to **Me**, and switch on **Send notifications here**. Allow notifications when your phone asks, then tap **Send a test** to check.
3. Or use Telegram

Under **Me**, enter your Telegram username, tap **Connect Telegram**, and press Start in the Zyra bot within 15 minutes. Then choose where notifications go: app and Telegram, app only, or Telegram only. Send /stop to the bot any time to disconnect.
When reminders arrive
By default, one reminder the day before. You can have up to three, anywhere from 14 days before to the start time — and change them for a single session under “Reminders for this session”.
A nudge from a lead
Leads can tap **Send reminder** on a session to nudge whoever's on it, with a short note like “Doors open at 8:30 this week.” It can be sent once an hour per session, so it never turns into spam.

items.q: Do reminders come by email?
items.a: No. Email is only for signing in and account security. Reminders come as phone notifications or Telegram messages.

items.q: I'm not getting notifications on my iPhone.
items.a: Make sure you opened Zyra from the home-screen icon, not Safari, and that notifications are allowed for it in Settings.

guides.title: QR or code check-in
guides.standfirst: Know who's actually there without a clipboard. Turn on check-in, show a code at the door, and get told early when someone hasn't arrived.
guides.meta_title: QR code and code check-in for sessions | Zyra
guides.meta_description: Turn on check-in for a space, show a changing code or QR at the venue, optionally check location, and get alerts when someone misses one.

blocks.title: The short version
blocks.text: In space **Settings** › “Check in and out”, turn the **Check-in button** on. For proof people are really there, add **Ask for a check-in code** and show it from the group's settings with **Show code**.
Turning it on

items: **Check-in button** — Off, On or Required. It appears from an hour before a session until it ends.
**Ask for a check-in code** — a four-character code that changes every 5 minutes, every hour or every day.
**Check the location too** — people must be near the group's venue (50 m to 5 km).
**Check-out button** — for when you also need finishing times.
**Tell me when someone misses one** — leads are told 10 minutes after the start.

blocks.text: At the door

A lead opens the group's settings and taps **Show code** (it's also on the Dashboard). People tap **Check in** on their session and type the code, or tap **Scan the QR instead** to scan it from the screen.
Forgotten phones
If the space allows it, owners and leads can mark someone checked in or out by hand, with a reason, so records stay honest.
Privacy
With the location check on, Zyra stores only how far someone was from the venue, never their actual position. After five wrong codes in ten minutes, check-in pauses briefly to stop guessing.

items.q: Do people need a separate scanner app?
items.a: No. The scanner is built into Zyra.

items.q: Can I use check-in without codes?
items.a: Yes — the button alone works for teams that trust each other and just want a record.

guides.title: Plans, seats and Unlimited
guides.standfirst: Free for small teams, seats for bigger spaces, and Unlimited for people who serve in many teams. Here is how the pieces fit.
guides.meta_title: Zyra plans: Free, seats and Unlimited | Zyra
guides.meta_description: What the free plan includes, how seats work when a space grows, what Unlimited adds, and how to pay monthly, yearly or once.

blocks.title: The short version
blocks.text: Joining and using Zyra is free. A space is free up to a set number of people; beyond that, its owner adds seats. Unlimited is a personal plan for people in lots of groups — and they never take up a seat.
Personal plans

blocks.caption: See and change yours under **Me** › Plan.
rows: Join as many as you like
Join as many as you like
Uses a seat in a space
One small ad on the home screen

blocks.text: Unlimited can be paid monthly or yearly, or once for life when that option is offered. Prices are shown on the Plan screen and on Zyra's pricing page.
Seats in a space

Each space is free up to a set number of people. When it grows past that, the owner goes to **Settings** › “People and seats” › **Add seats**, one at a time or in packs, charged for the time left in the period. People on Unlimited don't use a seat at all.
Managing billing

items: **Manage billing** under Plan updates your card, switches monthly or yearly, or cancels.
Have a promo code? Enter it under Plan and tap **Apply**.
Cancel a paid plan before deleting your account.

items.q: Does my whole team need Unlimited?
items.a: No. Most members are fine on Free. Unlimited suits people who serve in several groups.

items.q: What happens if a space is full?
items.a: New people see “This space is full” and can let the owner know they're waiting. Adding seats lets them in.

guides.title: Keeping your account safe
guides.standfirst: Two-step sign-in is always on in Zyra. Here is how it works, how to use an authenticator app instead of email codes, and how to delete your account.
guides.meta_title: Two-step sign-in and account safety | Zyra
guides.meta_description: How Zyra's always-on two-step sign-in works, switching to an authenticator app, managing remembered devices, and deleting your account.

blocks.title: The short version
blocks.text: On a new device, Zyra emails you a 6-digit code to confirm it's you. Tick **Remember this device** on your own phone. For extra safety, turn on an authenticator app under **Me** › Your account.
How two-step sign-in works

After your password, a new device shows “Confirm it's you” and Zyra emails a 6-digit code that lasts 10 minutes. Tick **Remember this device** on a phone or computer only you use, and you won't be asked again there for a while.
Using an authenticator app
Under **Me** › Your account › Authenticator app, tap **Turn on** and scan the code with your authenticator. From then on you can confirm sign-ins with the app instead of waiting for an email.
Lost a phone?

items: Under **Me** › Your account, open **Remembered devices** and forget the lost one.
Tap **Sign out others** to end every session except the one you're using.
Change your password with **Change** — Zyra emails you a link.

blocks.text: Deleting your account

Under **Me** › Your account, type DELETE and tap **Schedule deletion**. You have 14 days to change your mind. Cancel any paid plan first. Spaces you own pass to a lead, and your past messages show as “Former member”.

items.q: Can I turn two-step sign-in off?
items.a: No. It protects everyone's roster and contact details, so it's always on.

items.q: I didn't get the code.
items.a: Check your spam folder and that the email address is right. Codes expire after 10 minutes, so ask for a new one if it's been a while.
